nodes.label: HLS heal: rewrite a dead segment host to the playlist's own gateway host
nodes.norm_label: hls heal rewrite dead segment host to the playlist's own gateway host
nodes.summary: When an HLS playlist resolves fine but every segment host is dead, the host that served the playlist usually also serves the same segment paths. Rewriting each absolute segment URL to the playlist URL's own host, saving the playlist locally, and playing that file repairs playback without touching the player or the provider's binary.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L2872] The replacement host is not a hardcoded mirror list; it is taken from the playlist URL ani-cli just handed over, which had already answered successfully that second, so it is known alive for this session and no hostname is guessed

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L2870] If the heal fails for any reason the wrapper still execs the player on the original URL, so the wrapper can never be worse than having no wrapper at all

nodes.label: A Cloudflare-suspended edge CDN kills only the sub stream while the dub stream plays
nodes.norm_label: a cloudflare-suspended edge cdn kills only the sub stream while the dub stream plays
nodes.summary: For One Piece on hianime.at there is a single server, Vidstream-2 (MegaPlay). Its sub (Japanese audio) segments were served from an edge host that 302-redirects to cloudflare-terms-of-service-abuse.com and 404s, while the dub (English audio) segments went to a different, live host and played normally. The symptom reads as a broken subtitle setting; the cause is a provider-side ToS suspension of one edge host.

nodes.label: Audio-based subtitle sync fails on music-heavy media; sub-to-sub against the stream's own caption works
nodes.norm_label: audio-based subtitle sync fails on music-heavy media; sub-to-sub against the stream's own caption works
nodes.summary: alass run against extracted stream audio (cold open, OP theme and constant BGM give false voice activity) shifted subtitle blocks by plus or minus 39 seconds and collapsed the opening cues onto 0:00:00.00. Running alass subtitle-to-subtitle against the English caption ani-cli already extracted from the same stream shifted the 300-cue main block by 0.000 and corrected only the 9 tail cues, so an already-correct subtitle is left alone.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L4520] The audio run's output is self-refuting: four consecutive cues all start at 0:00:00.00, which cannot be right

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L4707] The sub-to-sub run reports shifted block of 300 subtitles with length 0:22:50.450 by 0:00:00.000, so the body of the episode is provably untouched

nodes.label: Comparing playlist EXTINF total against subtitle span rules out framerate drift
nodes.norm_label: comparing playlist extinf total against subtitle span rules out framerate drift
nodes.summary: Summing every EXTINF in the media playlist gives the true video duration; comparing it with the subtitle file's last event gives a ratio. A 1.002 ratio excludes a 25 versus 23.976 fps mismatch, which would show as roughly 1.043 or 0.959, so a global --sub-speed correction is the wrong tool and would only move about 3 seconds at the end.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L03480] Video 1477.86s against a last subtitle event at 1474.6s is a 0.2% difference, and a PAL mismatch would appear as a 4% gap, so the two timelines are not off by a scaling factor

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L03707] Stated as the conclusion carried into the user-facing answer: this is not a framerate problem, so --sub-speed globally would only correct about 3 seconds

nodes.label: ffmpeg's HLS demuxer does not forward the referrer to segment requests
nodes.norm_label: ffmpeg's hls demuxer does not forward the referrer to segment requests
nodes.summary: A local playlist whose segment URLs are absolute is read by ffmpeg under a file-scheme protocol whitelist (file,crypto,data), so https segment requests are refused outright. Adding https to the whitelist gets past that, but every segment then returns 403 because neither -referer nor -headers reaches the child requests, even though fetching one segment directly with the same flags succeeds. mpv's --referrer does propagate, which is why mpv plays the healed playlist and ffmpeg cannot.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L4124] The control case: the same segment URL opened with only -referer exits 0, so the host is reachable and the failure is specific to the HLS path

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L4167] First gate is the local-file protocol whitelist, which blocks https before any request is made

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L4266] After widening the whitelist every segment fails 403, which is the referrer not being propagated

nodes.label: Sub-second mpv HLS stutter is readahead depth, not bandwidth
nodes.norm_label: sub-second mpv hls stutter is readahead depth, not bandwidth
nodes.summary: Four segments were measured at roughly 2 to 3.6 MB/s, about 22x realtime, so the gateway has bandwidth to spare. mpv's default demuxer-readahead-secs is 1, which fetches HLS segments just in time and stalls at each segment boundary; raising cache-secs and demuxer-readahead-secs to prebuffer about 30 seconds is what removes the stutter.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L3113] Measured segment throughput of about 2.3 MB/s on a roughly 11 second segment rules bandwidth out as the cause

[05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-29 - ani-cli-indo-playback-fix [ses_f118969a0ffeRaBW3S6qal4B5G].md:L3129] The conclusion drawn from those numbers: bandwidth is not causing the stutter, the bottleneck is inside mpv

nodes.label: Git history cannot prove a runtime cause
nodes.norm_label: git history cannot prove a runtime cause
nodes.summary: The user reported playback working at the first push to a private repo. All four commits in that repo fall inside a 23-minute window on 2026-09-29 and none of them changes video or patch behaviour, the installed wrapper is byte-identical to the repo copy, and the vendored patched ani-cli is byte-identical to the active /usr/local/bin binary. The playback change therefore cannot be attributed to the repo; the plausible cause is upstream, on the provider's side.

nodes.label: Telegram pref storage is a flat per-installation table, so the gate is per-OS-user and not per-Snipset-account
nodes.norm_label: telegram pref storage is a flat per-installation table, so the gate is per-os-user and not per-snipset-account
nodes.summary: The button renders only when the telegram_bot_token preference is a non-empty string, read by useClipboardHistory and useClipboardDataLoader with render guards in ClipboardMagicMenuItem and ClipboardCard. The token lives in a flat per-installation key/value table (database/schema.rs:65-68), so the gate is per OS user, not per Snipset account and not per cloud profile. Verdict BY-DESIGN: the user-requested item was per-user Telegram and that is what it is.
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t1-clipboard-code-audit [ses_f1b184b00ffeWsjIRJDISmNquG].md:L8356] Flat per-installation SQLite storage is why the gate resolves to per-OS-user and not to a Snipset account, which is what makes the item by-design rather than a defect

nodes.label: Clipboard embedding search is gated off, deadline-capped and silently falls back to LIKE with no tests
nodes.norm_label: clipboard embedding search is gated off, deadline-capped and silently falls back to like with no tests
nodes.summary: services/embedding_search.rs is called from the clipboard history query and gated off by the ai_semantic_search preference, hard-capped at a 500 ms Ollama deadline, and on timeout falls back silently to plain keyword LIKE ranking. The file has no #[cfg(test)] module at all and no test exercises the clipboard semantic branch, so the integration is wired but unverified.
